10: A strong frame shows a clearly readable spider silhouette centered in view, with all eight legs distinguishable and mid-stride at different phases. Score each criterion 1-5. (1) Anatomy readability: body segments and eight two-part legs are identifiable. (2) Gait plausibility: legs sit in visibly different phases, some lifted and some planted. (3) Composition: the whole spider is framed with margin, camera at a three-quarter angle, nothing cropped. (4) Lighting and shadow: soft light, a contact or cast shadow grounding the feet, with material contrast between body and legs. (5) Polish: consistent colors, no z-fighting or detached joints, feet touch the ground.
11: A strong frame reads instantly as a pendulum clock. Score each criterion 1-5. (1) Clock legibility: face, 12 marks and three hands are crisp and distinguishable, and the time shown is plausible. (2) Pendulum readability: rod and weighted bob are visible and off-center, which implies swing. (3) Composition: the whole clock is centered with headroom, with no cropping and a roughly front-facing view. (4) Materials and lighting: wood tones against brass or metal parts, warm light, soft shadows, visible depth in the case. (5) Polish: proportions look like a real tall clock, parts are aligned, no clipping or floating pieces.
12: A strong frame shows a recognizable bird mid-flap over a grounded scene. Score each criterion 1-5. (1) Bird readability: body, head, beak and tail are clear, and the wing bend is visible. (2) Motion cues: wings are at a clear mid-flap pose with a bank angle, so the frame implies movement. (3) Composition: the bird is large enough in frame (at least 8% of canvas area), with props and ground giving scale, and is not cropped. (4) Lighting and color: a sky-colored background, a shadow on the ground under the bird, and good color contrast between the bird and its backdrop. (5) Polish: parts are joined without gaps, proportions are cohesive, and the scene is not empty or flat.
